background_setup.summary: # Introduction Audio language models are now widely used for various audio understanding problems, especially temporal tasks that require grounding in the audio content .

prior_work_limitation.summary: Firstly, audio LMs are prone to hallucinations, as multimodal LMs are typically constructed by coupling a modalityspecific encoder with an LM decoder and have been observed to ignore the audio input in favor of the text prompt .

evidence.quote: Firstly, audio LMs are prone to hallucinations, as multimodal LMs are typically constructed by coupling a modalityspecific encoder with an LM decoder and have been observed to ignore the audio input in favor of the text prompt (Ahia et al., 2025; Sakshi et al., 2025).

prior_work_limitation.summary: Relatedly, audio LMs often memorize the text of the timestamps in the training data and struggle with length generalization, leading to large errors when predicting timestamps that fall outside of its training window (e.g., if all audio examples in training...

evidence.quote: Relatedly, audio LMs often memorize the text of the timestamps in the training data and struggle with length generalization, leading to large errors when predicting timestamps that fall outside of its training window (e.g., if all audio examples in training are less than n minutes long, then the model will not predict positions greater than n minutes).

prior_work_limitation.summary: It is computationally inefficient, replacing what should be a simple pointer to the audio sequence with an expensive auto-regressive process (e.g., generating 7–10 tokens for a single word-level timestamp for a range like ‘[2.39, 4.11]’).

evidence.quote: It is computationally inefficient, replacing what should be a simple pointer to the audio sequence with an expensive auto-regressive process (e.g., generating 7–10 tokens for a single word-level timestamp for a range like ‘[2.39, 4.11]’).

core_problem_transition.summary: Because the text decoder is unconstrained, it can generate timestamps that are syntactically correct but have no correspondence to the audio content.

core_problem_transition.summary: Because the decoder does not learn to map audio features to textual representations of time beyond its training distribution, the generated timestamps for these later segments are effectively ungrounded.

method_transition.summary: In our framework, the model learns to reuse its audio representations (including decoder outputs that are normally discarded, because they are not needed for token generation) to produce a probability distribution over audio frames for a given audio event...
